message:
feat: exact-phrase boost, MyAPI classifier alias, synthesized_note guard

Three trust-pass patches that closed the blocker query set:

- Exact-phrase boost with hyphen/space/no-space normalization
  (_exact_phrase_boost, _query_phrases, _phrase_variants). Title/file/
  alias hits = 0.40, body 3+ hits = 0.30, body 1+ = 0.22. Closes the
  F5/H4 regression where notes containing "gold mine" verbatim lost to
  semantically-noisy docs about "gold" or "mining" alone.

- MyAPI classifier alias added to _PROJECT regex, _specialized_anchor_
  bonus, _anchor_terms_from_query, _expand_query_for_retrieval. Lifts
  A1 from weak win (LlamaIndex thread #1) to clean win (anchor #1).

- broken/blocked/failing/issue operational patterns added to
  _OPERATIONAL. OPERATIONAL reordered before PROJECT so "broken in
  MyAPI" routes to operational, not project_overview.

- end-to-end SYNTHESIS regex now matches hyphenated form.

- _infer_document_kind synthesized_note branch now excludes chat-dump
  sources (chatgpt/claude/claude-code/codex). Prevents tangential
  ChatGPT threads with "overview" in title from inheriting the +0.14
  synthesized_note prior in project/synthesis intents.

Verified on instance-20260418-024637: F5/H4/A1/A2/A3/A7 all pass.

author: Saboor Khurshid Chaudry
message:
feat(normalizer): add source field, --strip-format, --write-source-default, coverage ledger

Updates the V4 normalizer for the next phase of vault migration:

- Add `source` to APPLY_FIELDS and FIELD_ORDER. Suggest `original` for
  04 Periodic notes and `imported` for everything else when missing.
  Preserve existing source if valid.

- Add `log` and `utility` to VALID_TYPES; add `incubating` to
  PROJECT_EVENT_STATUSES. Now matches the V4 schema's full enums.

- Update TOP_LEVEL_MAP so `09 Utilities/` and `Templates/` default to
  type=utility (was incorrectly mapping to resource).

- Change inferred areas to match V4 templates: `04 Periodic` →
  [[Life]] (was [[System]]); `09 Utilities` → [[Vault]] (was [[System]]).

- Apply phase enforces V4 structural rules:
  - migration_status flips from `v4-dry-run` to `v4-applied`.
  - `format:` stripped (default; --no-strip-format to opt out).
  - `status:` stripped from non-project/event types (unconditional V4 rule).
  - source default backfilled (default; --no-write-source-default to opt out).
  - Unprefixed tags preserved (owner-pass territory, not auto-edited).

- New `append_coverage_ledger` writes to project-docs/coverage-ledger.json
  on every --apply run. Solves the "no central ledger" gap from prior
  batches — the ledger now records batch name, subdir, applied/skipped
  counts, manifest path, and flag state per run.

- New CLI flags: --strip-format/--no-strip-format,
  --write-source-default/--no-write-source-default, --batch, --ledger.

Validated end-to-end against ~/Repos/vault-doctor/mock_vault/ across
all eight V4 type zones (inbox, projects, areas, resources, periodic,
archive, utilities, plus already-applied state). All expected behaviors
confirmed: format/status strip, source backfill, area/project inference,
type override for utilities, no-frontmatter handling, body preservation,
backups, manifests, ledger.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(scripts): per-batch concept suggestion cheat sheets

For each Phase 4 batch, scan every note's body against keyword patterns
matching the 21 seeded concept stubs. Emit a per-batch markdown table
sorted by review/medium/high confidence: note path → top 3 suggested
concepts → hit counts.

Purpose: speed up owner-pass. Instead of fresh judgment per note, the
operator glances at the cheat-sheet row and confirms the suggestion
in the CLI. Most rows become one-keystroke decisions.

Generated 15 cheat sheets covering 1376 notes (~80% of the vault) with

- "Useful Git Commands" → [[Multi-Device Git Workflow]] @ 136 hits
- "VISION_B_PLAN" → [[Raspberry Pi]] @ 19, [[CLI Workflow]] @ 9
- "transcript-Danger-Illusion-of-AI-Code" → [[Programming]] @ 37

author: Saboor (BigPi)
message:
fix(retrieval): keyword lane skips bare-term filter when phrases present

KeywordSearcher required every bare term in the query to appear in the
document body, in addition to any quoted phrase. For long natural-language
queries containing a phrase (e.g. F5: 'Find the note where I used the term
"gold mine"'), this killed eligibility for the actual answer document — the
Trust-Threshold plan contains "gold mine" but obviously not "find", "where",
"used", "term".

When a phrase is given, treat it as the user's explicit intent and drop the
bare-term AND filter. Terms still influence ranking via match-density, just
not eligibility. Non-phrase queries are unaffected.

Closes F5 regression documented in run-2026-05-02-tighten-pass.md.
Acceptance set: 4/5 → 5/5 mechanical, no other queries moved.

author: Saboor (BigPi)
message:
fix(retrieval): keyword lane normalizes phrase separator variants

KeywordSearcher's eligibility check matched phrases via case-insensitive
substring lookup but ignored hyphen/space/no-space variants. The reranker's
exact-phrase boost normalizes those variants downstream, but only for
candidates already in the set — so docs containing "goldmine" (one word)
or "gold-mine" (hyphenated) were silently filtered out before they ever
reached the boost logic.

Add KeywordSearcher._phrase_variants (mirrors ResultReranker._phrase_variants
but always returns the original even for short phrases, since eligibility
must not return empty). Update both the eligibility check and the density
calc to iterate variants.

Discovered via multi-turn iterative probe of the gold-mine theme on
2026-05-03 (post-handoff): user remembered an OpenClaw thread containing
"goldmine"; ground-truth grep found 4 claude-source docs with the phrase
across spellings, but the API surfaced only 2. Variant fix closes the gap.

Side effect: F5 sentinel now FAILs in acceptance because the expanded
candidate set re-ranks. New top is chatgpt-project-shift-analysis.md;
Trust-Threshold plan slides to #7. The actual original-usage doc
(claude-web-converting-opclaw-to-final-system-repo.md) is at #3 —
arguably the right answer for "find the note where I used 'gold mine'"
since it contains the actual usage, not just meta-commentary about it.
F5's bank gold-doc may itself need updating; not done in this commit.
